definition: means a facility provided to the health insurance policyholders (including all members under family cover), to transfer the credits gained for, pre-existing diseases and specific waiting periods from one insurer to another insurer.
plain: Moving your health policy to a different insurer without losing the waiting periods you have already served.
whyItMatters: This is what stops a bad insurer from holding you hostage. You keep your continuity credit, so switching after three years does not mean serving the pre-existing-disease wait again. It has to be started well before renewal — usually 45 days — and the new insurer can still underwrite you, so it is a right to be considered, not a guarantee of acceptance.
